correctness.rationale: Direct derivation of donor-neighbor means yields the sharp interval for always-responsive center and frozen leaves. The exact iid affine recursion then gives all-time full-range oscillation by independent arbitrary-length edge runs. A stationary two-sided coupling proves uniqueness, ergodic occupation and a geometric Wasserstein bound; binary expansion gives a continuous uniform law at half-compromise, a 2^t-atom uniform finite law and the exact integrated quantile distance. Eight-hundred-eight direct rational edge-update tests, 27 exact finite-law/Wasserstein comparisons and eight stationary moment identities passed. Finite tests are only corroboration.

The stronger-looking heterogeneous DW convergence theorem applies only to direct distances, not neighbor-conditioned directionally asymmetric eligibility. Bernoulli convolutions themselves are classical and are explicitly credited; their model-specific emergence is the contribution. published-finding corpus and accessible prior research records comparisons did not reveal a subsuming claim; unindexed specialist notes remain a priority risk.

value.rationale: A published confidence rule allows persistent nonconvergence on the smallest connected graph despite homogeneous parameters and no designated stubborn agents. The explicit nonempty parameter wedge shows it is robust, while exact liminf/limsup and uniform ergodic occupation explain why numerical time traces can fluctuate indefinitely even as laws converge. The exact finite-time dyadic Wasserstein formula and total-variation obstruction distinguish distinct scientifically relevant forms of convergence. This is a natural structural boundary, not a parameter renaming.
